overview: This Senate resolution honors Corporal Grade One Matthew T. "Ty" Snook, a 10-year member of the Delaware State Police who was killed in the line of duty on December 23, 2025. He was shot while working an overtime assignment protecting employees and the public at a Division of Motor Vehicles facility near New Castle, Delaware, and the resolution notes that even after being mortally wounded he helped push an employee out of harm's way. It describes his work training more than 20 troopers and coaching young people. The resolution offers condolences to his family and reaffirms the Senate's support for law enforcement officers. The Senate agreed to it on February 3, 2026.
for: Supporters say the resolution rightly recognizes an officer who gave his life protecting others and reminds the country of the risks police face every day.
against: Critics say the resolution is symbolic and does not change any law or provide any support or funding for officers or their families.
